content.title: Activist investor HoldCo planning board fight at Comerica, WSJ reports
content.summary: The move comes just over a month after the South Florida-based asset manager pushed Comerica to pursue a sale process, saying the bank's stock has underperformed over the past two decades.  If the bank doesn't pursue a sale, HoldCo plans to nominate around five directors to Comerica's board when the window opens, likely in December, the WSJ report said, citing people familiar with the matter.

content.title: Activist Investor Pushing to Sell Comerica, Will Seek Board Seats
content.summary: An activist investor plans to launch a board fight at  Comerica  intensifying pressure on the Texas-based regional bank to sell itself.  The campaign signals the growing impatience among investors for a long-awaited wave of consolidation among regional lenders, which are under pressure to merge in order to better compete with behemoths like JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America.  Hedge fund HoldCo Asset Management has argued that Comerica should explore a sale after years of underperformance.
